name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
summary: A cable isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi through shoulder extension with straight arms.

setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high cable pulley.
Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip at roughly shoulder width.
Step back a couple of feet to create tension on the cable, hinge forward slightly at the hips, and maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Engage your core and pull the attachment downward in a sweeping arc toward your thighs using your lats.
Squeeze your lats and depress your shoulder blades firmly at the bottom of the movement near your hips.
Slowly raise your arms back up along the same path until you feel a deep stretch in your lats, keeping your elbows fixed.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the bar down toward your thighs, and inhale as you return the bar back overhead.
cues: Drive your hands toward your pockets
Keep elbows softly unlocked but frozen in place
Depress your shoulders away from your ears

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows like a triceps pressdown
common_faults.correction: Keep a soft, fixed bend at the elbows throughout the entire movement so the shoulder joint does all the work.

common_faults.fault: Using torso momentum to rock back and forth
common_faults.correction: Brace your core and maintain a stable, motionless hip hinge.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward at the top
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades depressed and avoid letting the weight pull your shoulders into your ears.

precautions: Ensure the cable attachment carabiner is fully locked before pulling.
